Bob Dylan and Keith Richards on stage at Live Aid, JFK Stadium, Philadelphia, July 13, 1985.

Dylan had the job of closing the American half of the show, and he brought two Rolling Stones with him: Keith Richards and Ronnie Wood. The three of them stood at the front of the stage with acoustic guitars and played Ballad of Hollis Brown, When the Ship Comes In and Blowin' in the Wind.

It was not the smoothest set of the day. The stage was busy getting ready for the finale behind them and the three of them had trouble hearing each other. At one point Dylan broke a string and Ronnie Wood handed over his own guitar and kept going on air guitar until a roadie brought another.

Dylan also said, on stage, that he hoped some of the money could go to American farmers who were losing their land. Those words helped start Farm Aid, which held its first concert that September.

Love it or not, it is one of the most talked about moments of the whole day, and the picture says a lot. Keith with his arm in the air, Bob in the middle of it all.

If I had to become an Applied AI Engineer from zero, I wouldn't waste months collecting certificates. I'd follow one rule: build something at every stage, and make every project prove a real engineering skill.

Next, learn to make AI reliable. Build evaluation pipelines, regression tests and guarded agents with human approval. Add prompt injection defense, PII protection and automated quality checks. A demo that works once is easy. A system that keeps working is the real challenge.

Then move into production. Deploy APIs, build responsive streaming interfaces, add model routing, fallbacks, caching and observability. Track cost per request, latency and failure rates. Great AI products aren't just intelligent. They're fast, affordable and dependable.

Finally, ship three real applications and publish measurable case studies. Show how you reduced costs, improved accuracy or eliminated hallucinations. Certificates prove what you've studied. Deployed products prove what you can do. Prompt wrappers are a commodity. Engineering judgment is the moat.
